mcp_server.def: A small program that lets an AI assistant use an outside tool or data source through the Model Context Protocol, an open standard.

model.def: The trained AI system that produces text, images or other output. Products and agents are built on top of models.

agent.def: Software that uses a model to carry out multi-step tasks on its own, often by calling tools.

prompt.def: The instructions or text you give an AI model. A prompt template is a reusable one.

skill.def: A packaged set of instructions and files that teaches an AI assistant to do a specific task.

library.def: Reusable code that developers add to their own software.

dataset.def: A collection of data used to train or test AI models.

product.def: A finished AI app or service that you use directly, without writing code.

article.def: Writing about AI: a guide, tutorial or blog post.

paper.def: A research paper, usually from arXiv.

event.def: A conference, meetup, webinar or hackathon.

course.def: A course or a certification about AI. Its platform is listed under Platforms; tags say whether it gives a certification (a proctored exam) or a certificate of completion, and whether it is self-paced, instructor-led, a live event or an exam only.

other.def: An AI resource that fits none of the other types.

glossary.typeAssigned: Helper2 assigns the type from the source's data, keyword rules or an AI model, so it can be wrong.

license.def: The rules for using, changing and sharing the resource. Always read the license itself before relying on it.

open_source.def: The source code is public under a license that lets others use and modify it. It does not always mean free of charge.

tech_level.def: How much technical skill is needed to get started.

platform.def: Where it runs, for example web, desktop, mobile or command line.

popularity.def: Counts such as stars or downloads reported by one source. They are never combined into a single score.

provenance.def: Where a piece of information came from and when it was retrieved.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.lede: Help people find the right AI resource for their need, and show the proof behind every answer.

sections.title: Why Helper2.ai exists
paragraphs: New AI models, tools, agents, MCP servers and papers appear every day. General search engines mix them with marketing pages and old content, so it is hard to know what is real and current.
Helper2.ai searches only sources about AI, tells you which sources it searched, and shows where every result comes from and when it was checked.

sections.title: What we promise
items: Proof before opinion. The guide only recommends a resource when it can quote a real source that supports the choice.
Honest coverage. We list every source we search and show what each one returned. We do not claim to search the whole web.
No invented facts. We never fill in dates, popularity or other facts that no source stated.
Open by default. The source code is public under the Apache-2.0 license.
Privacy first. No ads, no tracking, and we never sell data.

sections.title: How we mark AI text
items: On the screen, every text written by an AI model has a label next to it: “AI-written” in the guide’s picks bar and on the guide’s reasons in the result list, “Model’s explanation” over a reason in the preview, “AI summary” and “Extracted by AI” on the resource page, and “Steps written by AI” in the setup guide.
In the page, the same text carries the HTML attribute data-ai-generated="true", and data-ai-model with the model name when we know it.
In our API, a guide answer has an aiContent object that names the provider, the models and the fields they wrote. Catalog values carry an origin such as AI_SUMMARY or AI_EXTRACTED.
Quotes, titles and links are never written by AI. They come from the sources.

sections.title: Who is behind it
paragraphs: Helper2.ai is an independent project by Silvio Incalza, a software engineer based in Switzerland. The AI guide runs on NVIDIA Nemotron models served by Nebius Token Factory.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: Helper2.ai collects as little as possible. You can search and ask the guide without an account. There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking cookies, and we never sell data.

sections.title: What we process and why
items: Your searches and guide questions: the text you type, used only to answer you. It is not linked to your account. Search results are cached for up to 30 minutes and guide answers for up to 24 hours, keyed by the question. Please do not type personal or secret information.

Your account, if you sign in with GitHub: your GitHub user ID (a number), your display name and when you last signed in. We ask GitHub only for basic profile access. We never see your GitHub password or your e-mail address.

Saved items: if you are signed in, each saved resource (its link, title and type) and when you saved it, stored on our server with your account. If you are not signed in, they stay only in your browser; when you sign in, they move to your account.
Reports you send about a resource: the text you write, linked to your account if you are signed in.
Web search counters: Tavily searches per day and feature, under a keyed hash of your IP address and the date (no address stored; days cannot be linked), or your account ID once account limits are on.
Stored Tavily results, under a keyed hash of the question, not its text.

Technical data: your IP address is kept in memory for a short time to limit abuse (rate limits). Our servers and our web gateway also write technical logs, which can include your IP address and the pages you request. We keep these logs for up to 3 months to keep the service running and secure, then delete them.

sections.title: Legal basis
items: Answering your searches and guide questions, your account and your saved items: to provide the service you ask for (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
Rate limits, technical logs and the security cookie: our legitimate interest in keeping the service secure and available (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Web search counters and stored results: legitimate interest in a free service at bounded cost (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Reports you send: our legitimate interest in keeping the information on Helper2.ai correct (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

sections.title: Cookies and browser storage
items: A session cookie, only when you sign in, so you stay signed in.
A security cookie (XSRF-TOKEN) that protects forms against cross-site request forgery.

Browser storage for your language, your light or dark theme, the AI tool you chose in the setup guide and, if you are not signed in, your saved items. This data stays in your browser and is not sent to us.
All of these are strictly necessary for the site to work. We use no advertising, analytics or third-party cookies.

sections.title: Who receives data
items: Search sources: to find results, your search text is sent to the sources that answer live, such as GitHub, Hugging Face, npm, arXiv and Tavily. The Sources page lists them all. Each provider handles the request under its own privacy policy, and some of them are in the United States.
Tavily (United States): your search text or the guide's web query, unless a stored result answers.

AI models: guide questions, and searches written in a language other than English, are sent to NVIDIA Nemotron models on Nebius Token Factory, processed in the European Union. We send only the text, never your account data.
GitHub, when you choose to sign in with it.

Transfers abroad: some search sources, and GitHub, are in the United States. Where a provider is certified under the Swiss-US and EU-US Data Privacy Framework, the transfer relies on that certification. Otherwise, we send your search text abroad only because it is needed to give you the results you asked for (Art. 17(1)(b) FADP, Art. 49(1)(b) GDPR).
Hosting: our servers are in Germany (European Union).

sections.title: How long we keep data
items: Cached searches and guide answers: up to 30 minutes and 24 hours.
Technical logs: up to 3 months.
Web search counters: 24 hours. Stored results: 7 days.
Your account and saved items: until you delete them, or 24 months after you last signed in. Then we delete the account and its saved items.
Reports: 12 months after they were handled. If your account is deleted, your reports stay without your name until then.
Database backups: 7 days. Anything deleted above is gone from the backups within 7 days.

sections.title: Deleting your account
paragraphs: When you are signed in, select your name at the top of the page, then "Delete my account". We delete your account and your saved items at once and sign you out. Reports you sent stay, without your name. Signing in again later creates a new, empty account.
You can also write to the address above and we will delete it for you.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP) and, where it applies, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you can ask what data we hold about you, and ask us to correct, delete or export it. Write to the address above. You can also complain to the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) or to the data protection authority in your country.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: If this notice changes, we update this page and the date at the top.

how.title: How the guide answers
how.lede: Retrieval first, Nemotron second, a validator last. The model never decides what is true.

search.title: Search real sources
search.body: A fast Nemotron model turns your words, in any language, into search terms. A normal search across every source then finds up to 12 real candidates.

choose.title: Nemotron chooses
choose.body: A reasoning model picks at most 3 of those candidates, explains why with a quote, and can adapt a ready-to-use prompt from catalog prompts.

check.title: A validator checks
check.body: Each pick must be one of the candidates, and its quote must appear word for word in that resource’s text. Rejected suggestions are counted and shown.

notStated.title: Missing means unknown
notStated.body: If no source gave a fact, it says Unknown. Dates, popularity and prices are never filled in.

dates.title: Dates are the source’s own
dates.body: Published and updated come from the source. Otherwise you see when Helper2.ai first saw it.

unchecked.title: Every explanation is labelled
unchecked.body: Code checks the quote word for word. A second model call checks the explanation; the page says if it was checked, removed or not checked.

fallback.title: Search keeps working
fallback.body: If the AI model is unavailable, the guide shows the top real results instead, clearly labelled.
